clutter.issue: Large 'SECTOR 1 Outer Drift' title text overlays the upper-middle combat lane right where the first wave of enemies and bullets appear (00.0-01.0s).
Scrolling vertical dashed lane lines and orange dots on the floor add visual noise behind small pink bullets throughout the clip.
The 'Codex: Scout' banner (06.0-09.5s) and floating 'PETAL' tags on enemies (06.5-10.5s) sit directly in the combat lane alongside enemy ships and bullets.
The charging glow on the player ship is very bright and large, partially obscuring the ship's exact hitbox center.

The darker grey floor with scrolling dashed road-like markings adds slight visual texture under the small enemies and bullets compared to X's cleaner blue floor, though enemy pink outlines remain readable.
When the enemy fires a glowing pink bullet close to the charging player ship, the bright cyan charge flare overlaps the incoming pink projectile just before impact at 5.6s.

The player taking damage creates a huge bright white flash over the ship and nearby enemies/bullets without a screen-edge damage indicator, obscuring nearby pink bullets and looking like an attack explosion.
The large white flash when the player is hit still obscures the ship and nearby pink bullets around 1.0-1.2s, though the red screen border helps clarify what happened.
Scrolling orange and blue dots on the lane floor add minor visual noise underneath the pink enemies and bullets, though they remain dimmer than threats.
Bright white flash around the player ship when releasing a charged shot briefly obscures nearby pink enemy bullets.
The bright white charge-ready burst around the player ship is very large and momentarily obscures nearby enemy bullets.
Scrolling vertical road-like lane lines and yellow dots on the floor add visual noise behind small pink bullets, whereas Y has a cleaner, darker floor.
The grey lane surface has dashed road-like markings and small dark/orange scrolling specks that add visual noise behind pink enemy bullets and enemies, compared to the cleaner blue lane in Clip X.

The massive bright white flash and expanding ring from firing the charged shot right in front of approaching enemies and bullets momentarily obscures an incoming pink enemy bullet, leading to the player getting hit at 0:03.
The bright white flash around the player ship when releasing the charged shot briefly obscures the ship's exact hitbox.
Scrolling vertical dashed lane markings and faint circles on the track floor add visual noise that competes with small enemy bullets and target indicators throughout the clip.
When losing a life, a harsh, opaque-looking red rectangular border flashes around the entire screen, briefly distracting from the active bullets and enemies inside the lane.
The bright, saturated orange-brown floor fill across the entire play lane competes visually with the bright ship glow, white/cyan charge rings, and red warning text from 0:00 to 0:06.
The loud, harsh metallic screech/roar during the boss arrival (0:02 to 0:03) completely masks the shot impact sound.
Same loud metallic boss arrival screech at 0:02 to 0:03 overpowering combat audio cues.
Bright scrolling vertical white dashes on the floor and heavier bloom on the ship and scan cone compete visually with the small green projectiles.
The warm orange-brown floor reduces contrast with the pink enemy bullets slightly compared to X's darker floor, though small green projectiles are easier to spot without the white floor dashes.
Faint vertical dashed lines scrolling down the floor add minor visual noise compared to Y's clean floor, though bullets remain easy to see.
The warm reddish-orange floor color reduces contrast slightly with the pink/magenta enemy bullets and pink grazing rings compared to the darker grey floor in X.
When the ship charges and fires, the bright white/yellow bloom around the player ship is much larger than in X, momentarily obscuring nearby pink bullets right in front of the ship.
Scrolling vertical white dashes and yellow/green dots on the floor track add visual noise behind combat compared to the clean blue floor in X.
Disarmed grey enemy hulls stay on the playfield drifting downward, which can momentarily compete with active targets against the busier floor.
Full-screen red damage vignette is very intense and briefly obscures peripheral vision (also happens at 5.9s in X and 2.1s in Y).

overall.why: Clip Y has a clean, solid dark blue playfield without the scrolling dashed lines and orange floor dots seen in X, and it avoids blocking the initial enemy wave with large sector title text. Although X has a better red screen-border flash when losing a life, Y's cleaner background makes enemy bullets and ships easier to track overall.

Both clips use identical combat VFX, UI, and audio cues for charging, disarming, and taking hull damage, but Clip X's smoother, brighter blue track surface offers slightly cleaner contrast against the pink-outlined enemies and dark disarmed hulls than Clip Y's darker grey road-marked surface.

Clip Y is easier to read mainly because it adds a clear red screen-border flash when the player takes damage (at 1.0s and 6.0s), disambiguating player damage from the bright white explosion flash, and its scrolling floor markings provide much better spatial reference for ship movement than X's blank blue lane.

Clip Y is much easier to read as combat because it provides a clear on-ship aiming cone and audio buildup for charged shots, distinct visual rings and sound effects when enemies are hit or disarmed, and a cleaner playfield floor with less background texture noise.

Clip X has a cleaner, deeper blue lane background without the scrolling specks and dashed road lines seen in Clip Y, providing better contrast for pink enemy bullets and enemies. Clip X also clearly communicates enemy disarm states with on-screen 'NEUTRAL' labels and HUD notifications.

Clip Y removes the scrolling dashed lane lines and floor patterns present in Clip X, leaving a clean, solid dark surface inside the playfield. This significantly improves contrast for small pink enemy bullets, enemy ships, and targeting HUD elements. Additionally, the screen-edge damage indicator at t=4.5s in Y is a smoother vignette rather than X's harsh red border.

Clip Y features a much darker, desaturated track surface that gives significantly better contrast and visual separation for the player ship, charge rings, projectiles, and hit waves compared to the bright orange floor in Clip X.

Y removes the distracting scrolling white floor dashes and tones down the excessive bloom on the player ship and scanning cone (especially around 2.0s and 5.0s), making the small green projectiles and pink bullet patterns much cleaner and easier to read.

Clip X has better contrast between the dark grey track floor and the pink enemy bullets, and the player ship's charge/fire glow is more contained than in Y (where the bright flash at 0:04 briefly obscures nearby bullets).

Clip X has a clean, solid blue floor surface that gives maximum contrast to enemy bullets, red target rings, and the player's white aiming arc. Clip Y adds scrolling lane dashes and colored dots on the floor which slightly reduces contrast and adds background motion noise.
